title: Slot-based hiring cushion with price-velocity scan
content:
Executive summary:
This sheet captures a lightweight, stress-tested approach to aligning short-term hiring (4–12 week windows) with pricing experiments and throughput velocity. The idea: treat hiring capacity as discrete 'slots' (junior, mid, senior) that can be reserved, released, or accelerated based on a live pricing velocity signal. The playbook's goal is to limit permanent headcount commitments while preserving the ability to win revenue upcycles and control unit economics under price compression.

Why this is different:
- Fragments hiring into short-duration slots to match the bursty nature of hosted API demand and Dedicated seat ramps.
- Directly ties slot activation thresholds to pricing velocity (observed change in ARR-token price/throughput mix over trailing 14 days).
- Uses a graded buffer (soft, firm, hard) instead of a single cushion percent — reduces knee-jerk hiring.

Core assumptions (configurable inputs):
- Base monthly burn per FTE (all-in fully loaded): junior=13k, mid=18k, senior=30k (USD).
- Average token margin at current price mix: 38%.
- Pricing velocity signal = pct change in net effective price-per-token *weighted by route mix* over trailing 14 days. A +3% velocity for 14 days => slot activation.
- Slot durations: 6w (trial contractors), 12w (temp-to-hire), 52w (permanent).
- Max slot budget (quarterly): 15 slots across eng/infra/solutions.

Sensitivity framework (what we stress):
- Price drop scenarios: -5%, -10%, -20% over 12 weeks — observe margin, payback times, and required slot cancellations.
- Demand surge scenarios: +20%, +50% sustained 4 weeks — observe slot activation lag and estimated lost revenue if slots unavailable.
- Mix shift: embeddings-heavy vs chat-heavy route change; adjust token margin per route and recompute unit economics.

Modeled outputs (sample snapshot; figures illustrative):
- Baseline (no change): quarterly slot spend = $540k; expected incremental gross contribution (if filled and productive) = $720k; net delta = +$180k.
- Down -10% price: quarterly slot spend = $540k; expected incremental gross contribution = $520k; net delta = -$20k -> trigger: convert soft->firm cushion and freeze new slot activations.
- Up +35% demand (burst): incremental revenue opportunity = $1.1M over 8 weeks; with 6 available slots fillable within 3 weeks we capture ~70% of opportunity; without slots capture ~20%.

Quick computation snippets (cells we use in sheet):
- slot_cost_qtr = slots_filled * slot_duration_months * fte_burn_month
- expected_token_margin_delta = base_margin * (1 + price_delta_pct) * route_mix_factor
- payback_weeks = (revenue_from_slot * gross_margin) / (weekly_slot_cost)
- activation_flag = (rolling_price_velocity >= activation_threshold) AND (available_slots > 0)

Operational rules (playbook):
1) Soft cushion (default): maintain 10% headcount buffer of rotational/contract capacity. No automatic hiring; ops can approve 2-week contractors for urgent tasks.
2) Firm cushion (triggered): price-velocity > +3% for 14d OR demand > +25% for 7d. Approve up to 50% of slots as 12w temp-to-hire. Finance pre-allocates budget bucket and notifies recruiting.
3) Hard cushion (protect downside): price-velocity < -7% for 10d OR gross margin breach < 30% -> freeze discretionary hiring, convert open slots to contractor-only, and re-run scenario.

Governance and signals (what lives in console):
- live dashboard card: price_velocity_14d, route_mix_shift_index, avg_token_margin, open_slots_count, slot_fill_lag_days.
- weekly finance review: run 'Slot Sensitivity' tab (this sheet) and publish recommended actions to #finance-hiring channel.

Example 'Slot Sensitivity' tab layout (human-readable):
Row, Metric, Scenario A (baseline), Scenario B (-10%), Scenario C (+40% demand)
1, Slots filled, 8, 8, 12
2, Quarterly slot cost, $540,000, $540,000, $810,000
3, Incremental gross contribution, $720,000, $520,000, $1,320,000
4, Net delta, $180,000, -$20,000, $510,000
5, Payback weeks, 14, 22, 9

Mitigations and secondary levers:
- Dynamic pricing corridors: if velocity is negative but demand remains stable, tighten promotions on lower-margin routes first.
- Quick swap: convert open 12w temp slots into contractor benches within 5 business days to save ~30% of slot cost.
- Ops throttles: reduce burst autoscale headroom (Dedicated) for 48–72 hours while finance runs deeper analysis.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to reviewers):
- Accuracy of route_mix weighting — needs input from Product/Telemetry to map 6 canonical routes to token margin matrix.
- Recruiting pipeline realism: can recruiting deliver N=6 mid-level temps in 3 weeks without premium? (Recruiting: @Janelle to validate.)
- Contract/legal cost multipliers for non-US hires are currently placeholder +12%.

Action items (next 3 weeks):
- Priya: finalise slot cost model and publish sheet with live cell links to Console metrics (due 2026-12-09).
- Janelle: validate recruiter throughput and preferred vendor list (due 2026-11-20).
- Arjun: prototype the activation_flag webhook and demo in staging (JIRA-FT-8421) by 2026-12-03.

Appendix: short sensitivity grid (logic used by sheet)
- If net delta < -$50k for baseline quarter -> immediate hiring freeze and conversion of two mid slots to contractor bench.
- If payback_weeks <= 10 -> accelerate slot activation to permanent hire pathway.

Notes to self (drafty):
- Keep the sheet light and filterable by org-exposure (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Ensure conservative vacancy multipliers (assume 60% productivity first 6 weeks).
- Want a second sheet 'lost-opportunity-cost' that models revenue missed per unavailable slot per week (to make decisions quantitative).

Document history:

- v0.2 added governance and tie-to-console (2026-11-20 Liam)
- v0.3 sensitivity tweaks and action items (2026-12-02 Priya)

End of sheet.
